review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no @[simp] declarations, and no simp set, simp attribute or simp-normal-form lemma is defined or relied on. The only simp uses are local proof closers, such as `simp` for `μ ∅ ≠ ∞` and `simp only [add_thirds]`. The sibling file UniformIntegrable.lean, which this file follows, has no @[simp] attributes either. UnifTight is an unfolded ∀∃ predicate, and the iff lemmas (`unifTight_iff_real`, `unifTight_iff_nnreal`) are reformulations, not rewrite rules. Making them simp lemmas would be unjustified: they would introduce a cast or a different quantifier shape, and they carry no normal-form benefit. The private lemmas and the deprecated declarations are not part of the public simp interface. I found no rewrite cycle, no competing rules and no unwanted expansion. I did not run Lean, and I did not search every downstream user of UnifTight for places where a missing simp lemma would matter.
